problem: Achieving both optimality and adversarial robustness in deep reinforcement learning is difficult because robust policy optimization sacrifices returns.
approach: BARPO uses a bilevel framework that modulates adversary strength to balance robustness and performance while navigating the policy landscape more effectively.
contribution: BARPO consistently outperforms vanilla ARPO, reconciling the theory-practice gap between robust and standard policy optimization.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) for diffusion models relies on pairwise preferences, missing richer ranked preference information humans provide.
approach: Diffusion-LPO aggregates ranked lists of images per caption and derives a listwise DPO objective using the Plackett-Luce model to enforce consistency across rankings.
contribution: Diffusion-LPO consistently outperforms pairwise DPO on text-to-image, image editing, and personalized preference tasks.

problem: Existing text-to-image benchmarks fail to comprehensively evaluate both composition and reasoning across scene densities and complexity.
approach: T2I-CoReBench structures composition by scene graph elements (instance, attribute, relation) and reasoning by philosophical frameworks (deductive, inductive, abductive), creating a 12-dimensional taxonomy with 1,080 prompts and 13,500 checklist questions.
contribution: T2I-CoReBench provides comprehensive and fine-grained evaluation of composition and reasoning capabilities across diverse T2I models.

problem: Large monolithic time series foundation models are resource-intensive; smaller alternatives lack competitive performance.
approach: A portfolio of specialist models achieves competitive performance through ensembling or model selection, using post-training to diversify a base model with fewer parameters.
contribution: Specialist model portfolios achieve competitive large-scale benchmarks results while using much fewer parameters and being more compute-efficient than test-time fine-tuning.

problem: Model Context Protocol (MCP) for LLM agents standardizes tool access but enlarges the attack surface with little systematic evaluation of security.
approach: MSB introduces a taxonomy of 12 MCP-specific attacks (name-collision, prompt injection, parameter manipulation, etc.) and an evaluation harness executing real benign and malicious tools via MCP across 10 domains.
contribution: MSB evaluates 9 LLM agents across 405 tools with 2,000 attack instances, revealing vulnerability patterns and introducing Net Resilient Performance (NRP) to quantify the security-performance tradeoff.

problem: Multi-LM architectures with compressor-predictor designs lack principled guidance; attributing gains to compression versus prediction is costly.
approach: An information-theoretic framework models the compressor LM as a noisy channel and estimates mutual information between context and its compression to quantify quality task-independently.
contribution: Mutual information strongly predicts downstream performance independent of task, and larger compressors are 1.6× more accurate and 4.6× more token-efficient.

problem: First-last frame video generation suffers from semantic degradation and subject deformation in intermediate frames, undermining temporal consistency.
approach: Anchor Frame Bridging adaptively interpolates anchor frames at semantically critical locations using frame order reversal, then leverages them to guide semantic propagation across the sequence.
contribution: Applied to Wan2.1-I2V, AFB yields 16.58% FVD and 10.21% PSNR improvements without per-scene optimization.

problem: Cross-modal image translation using standard diffusion approaches forces samplers to traverse off-manifold regions, causing inefficiency and semantic drift.
approach: The method embeds domain-shift dynamics into the generative process by predicting spatially-varying mixing fields and injecting target-consistent restoration at each reverse step, keeping updates on-manifold.
contribution: Improved structural fidelity and semantic consistency across medical imaging, remote sensing, and electroluminescence tasks while converging in fewer denoising steps.

problem: Transformer-based PDE surrogates suffer from systematic error accumulation at harmonic frequencies due to fixed patch sizes, and have inflexible computational costs.
approach: Overtone dynamically modulates patch sizes during inference through cyclic stride or kernel modulation, distributing errors across the frequency spectrum and enabling compute-adaptive deployment.
contribution: A single Overtone model achieves up to 40% error reduction in long rollouts and matches or exceeds multiple fixed-patch baselines across all compute budgets on 2D and 3D PDEs.

problem: Positional encoding in Transformers lacks a unified geometric framework; existing methods (RoPE, ALiBi) are disconnected design choices.
approach: GRAPE unifies positional encoding through group actions: multiplicative rotations in SO(d) and additive logit biases from unipotent GL actions, subsuming RoPE and ALiBi as special cases.
contribution: GRAPE supplies a principled design space for positional geometry in long-context models with learned commuting subspaces and non-commuting mixtures at O(d) and O(rd) costs.

problem: Predictive coding networks use dense floating-point messages incompatible with neuromorphic hardware and spike-based computation.
approach: DiffPC replaces dense messages with sparse ternary spikes, provides spike-compatible target and error updates, and employs adaptive threshold schedules for event-driven operation.
contribution: Achieves 99.3% on MNIST, 89.6% on Fashion-MNIST, outperforms backpropagation on CIFAR-10, with over two orders of magnitude reduction in data movement.

problem: Understanding how LLMs perform logical reasoning through their representations is unclear; it is unknown whether reasoning is surface-level or genuinely internalized.
approach: A geometric framework models reasoning as flows (embedding trajectories) in representation space, using the same logical propositions with varied semantics to disentangle logic from form.
contribution: LLM reasoning corresponds to smooth flows whose velocities are locally controlled by logical statements, providing a geometric foundation and practical tools for interpretability analysis.

problem: Single prompt evolution is limited; aggregating multiple prompts via voting could improve system capability but few methods explore this.
approach: C-Evolve uses island-based evolutionary algorithms to discover groups of prompts whose aggregated outputs after majority voting optimize performance, using voting score as fitness instead of individual performance.
contribution: Achieves 70.67% on HotpotQA and 43.88% on IFBench (Qwen3-8B), 4.95% and 2.73% higher than GEPA; GPT-4.1-mini reaches 47.96% and 95.33% on MATH.

problem: Existing cluster validation indices ignore noise assignments in density-based clustering (DBSCAN, HDBSCAN), evaluating only cluster quality without assessing noise correctness.
approach: DISCO extends the Silhouette Coefficient using density-connectivity for arbitrary-shaped clusters and explicitly rewards correct noise labels while penalizing misclassified noise.
contribution: DISCO is the first CVI to assess noise assignment quality and handles edge cases like singleton clusters, enabling explainable clustering evaluation.

problem: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards optimized for text is suboptimal for multimodal reasoning, where 67% of errors stem from visual perception failures.
approach: PAPO introduces Implicit Perception Loss (KL divergence between distributions over original and corrupted visual inputs) and Double Entropy Loss regularization to encourage visually grounded reasoning without annotations.
contribution: Achieves 4.4%-17.5% overall improvements on multimodal benchmarks, with 8.0%-19.1% on vision-heavy tasks and 30.5% reduction in perception errors.

problem: Data synthesis must protect privacy and fairness for underrepresented groups, especially in data-scarce environments prone to bias amplification.
approach: A Bayesian nonparametric conditional generative model minimizes mutual information between generated outcomes and protected attributes, handling non-binary sensitive features and class imbalance systematically.
contribution: Provides privacy-preserving, fairness-aware data synthesis with theoretical guarantees for ethical and equitable generation of synthetic data.

problem: Canonicalization in equivariant networks introduces discontinuities affecting training stability, generalization, and universal approximation guarantees.
approach: Adaptive canonicalization makes the standard form depend on both input and network parameters by choosing the form to maximize network confidence, yielding continuous symmetry-respecting models.
contribution: Admits universal approximation and outperforms data augmentation, standard canonicalization, and equivariant architectures on molecular, protein, and point cloud tasks.

problem: Adaptive optimizers like AdamW lack coordinate interdependence capture; SOAP is more effective but memory-intensive for massive LLMs.
approach: COSMOS applies SOAP to the leading eigensubspace (primary optimization dynamics) and MUON to the remaining eigensubspace, leveraging different importance levels to balance memory and performance.
contribution: Significantly reduces memory consumption while maintaining robust optimization performance, making it particularly suitable for massive LLMs.

problem: Sampling from strongly log-concave distributions via Langevin dynamics with Euler-Maruyama discretization has high convergence complexity.
approach: The Poisson midpoint discretization for overdamped/underdamped Langevin dynamics achieves convergence in 2-Wasserstein distance with cubic speedup over Euler-Maruyama.
contribution: Demonstrates Wasserstein convergence complexity much smaller than existing L2 strong error lower bounds for underdamped dynamics.

problem: Existing time series forecasting methods capture coarse variable correlations but miss fine-grained, time-dependent variable interactions.
approach: FACT uses depth-wise convolutions with channel-specific kernels to model dynamic variable interactions, reconfigures 1D variables into 2D space, and applies multi-dilated convolutions with increasing dilation rates.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art forecasting accuracy and substantial efficiency gains, significantly reducing training time and memory compared to attention mechanisms.

problem: The Neural Feature Ansatz explains feature learning empirically but lacks theoretical grounding, making it unclear when it fails or how to improve it.
approach: Using first-order optimality conditions, FACT derives the Features at Convergence Theorem as a principled alternative that predicts what features emerge at convergence.
contribution: Achieves greater agreement with learned features, explains why NFA holds in most settings, and captures grokking and phase transitions in learning sparse parities.

problem: Automated theorem proving in formal languages is difficult; existing open-source provers lag far behind closed-source models in performance.
approach: Goedel-Prover-V2 combines expert iteration, reinforcement learning, scaffolded data synthesis during training plateaus, self-correction using compiler feedback, and checkpoint averaging for test-time exploration.
contribution: Goedel-Prover-V2-8B reaches 84.6% pass@32 on MiniF2F, outperforming DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B; the 32B model achieves 88.1% and 90.4% in self-correction mode, surpassing prior SOTA.

problem: It is unclear where and how LLMs store newly finetuned facts during learning—whether they enrich entity tokens or recall information just-in-time.
approach: Dynamic weight grafting selectively grafts weights from finetuned to pretrained models to identify two pathways: enriching residual streams at entity tokens and recalling at the final token via attention and feedforward networks.
contribution: Reveals separate enrichment and recall pathways for finetuned facts, with different tasks relying on one or both pathways, localizing recall to final-layer components.

problem: Pre-training RL agents is difficult because actions have long-term dependencies; existing foundation model approaches don't reason effectively across time.
approach: InFOM uses flow matching to predict occupancy measures (which states an agent visits in the future) and includes a latent variable capturing user intention for expressivity and task adaptation via generalized policy improvement.
contribution: InFOM achieves 1.8× median improvement in returns and 36% increase in success rates compared to alternative pre-training methods across 36 benchmark tasks.

problem: High-fidelity 3D editing typically requires per-scene optimization and multiple edited input views to ensure multi-view consistency.
approach: TINKER leverages pretrained diffusion models' latent 3D awareness via a multi-view consistent editor and an any-view-to-video scene completion model, requiring only one or two edited images as input.
contribution: Delivers robust multi-view consistent edits from minimal images without per-scene training, advancing scalable 3D and 4D content creation.

problem: Multimodal reasoning in MLLMs is confined to language space, treating visual information as static input rather than dynamically processing it during reasoning.
approach: Latent Visual Reasoning enables autoregressive reasoning directly in visual embedding space by training the model to generate latent states reconstructing critical visual tokens, interleaved with text generation and GRPO reinforcement learning.
contribution: Achieves 71.67% on MMVP compared to 66.67% with Qwen2.5-VL, substantially improving fine-grained visual understanding through latent visual reasoning.

problem: Inference scaling through resampling might allow weaker models to match stronger ones, but fundamental limits exist when verifiers have imperfect accuracy.
approach: Analysis shows that non-zero false positive rates in verifiers impose an upper bound to resampling accuracy regardless of compute budget; this correlates strongly with single-sample accuracy.
contribution: Optimal sampling attempts are often fewer than 10 as false positives' negative utility outweighs benefits, demonstrating fundamental limits on inference scaling with imperfect verifiers.

problem: Successor Measure is a powerful predictive object in RL but lacks compact representations tailored for online algorithms.
approach: SF2 leverages flow-matching generative models to approximate successor measures while enforcing structured decomposition into time-invariant embeddings and time-dependent projections, integrating into standard off-policy algorithms.
contribution: Improves sample efficiency and training stability compared to successor feature baselines on DeepMind Control Suite tasks through compact representation from flow matching.

problem: Existing image manipulation localization methods are task-specific; joint training on multiple IML tasks causes performance degradation, hindering real applications.
approach: Omni-IML uses a Modal Gate Encoder for adaptive modality selection, a Dynamic Weight Decoder for task-specific filter adjustment, and an Anomaly Enhancement module for task-agnostic feature learning, supported by the Omni-273k dataset with natural language descriptions.
contribution: First generalist model achieving state-of-the-art across all four major IML tasks without per-task designs, offering practical deployment value.

problem: Existing test-time domain generalization relies on coarse-grained style transfer, ineffective for pixel-level tasks like image super-resolution.
approach: MC-TTDG uses multi-codebook-based representation learning with domain-specific and domain-invariant codebooks, performs pixel-level nearest-neighbor feature matching, and uses voting-based selection for optimal codebook choice.
contribution: Effectively transfers feature distributions for SR networks with strong zero-shot generalization across diverse data distributions and network architectures.

problem: Understanding what drives few-step diffusion distillation is unclear; Distribution Matching Distillation's effectiveness is conventionally attributed to distribution matching.
approach: Decomposing DMD reveals CFG Augmentation as the core engine driving distillation while Distribution Matching acts as a regularizer; simpler constraints or GAN objectives can serve the same stabilizing function.
contribution: Decoupled understanding enables principled modifications like decoupling noise schedules for engine and regularizer, leading to improved performance.

problem: Multimodal learning assumes consistent modality availability, but source and target environments differ in which modalities are observed due to cost or hardware issues.
approach: ICYM2I formalizes the missingness problem and introduces inverse probability weighting-based correction to properly estimate information gain and predictive performance under missingness shifts.
contribution: Framework addresses distribution shift from modality missingness, demonstrating importance of missingness adjustment on synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real-world datasets.

problem: Extending Transformers to graph-structured data remains challenging; tokenizers are not available for graphs, preventing direct application of pretrained Transformers.
approach: Graph tokenization combines reversible serialization guided by substructure statistics with Byte Pair Encoding to generate sequential graph representations that capture structural information.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on 12 benchmarks, outperforming graph neural networks and specialized graph transformers without architectural modifications.

problem: Standard preference-based alignment assumes clean labels, but real-world preference datasets contain substantial label noise from annotators, inconsistency, and low-effort feedback.
approach: RPO uses Expectation-Maximization to infer posterior probability of each label's correctness and re-weight training data; generalizes to transform any preference loss into its robust counterpart.
contribution: Framework transforms existing alignment algorithms into robust versions, with convergence guarantees to true noise level under calibration and consistent effectiveness.

problem: Degradation-agnostic image restoration must balance efficiency and performance across diverse corruptions, but existing methods either sacrifice efficiency or fail to capture distinct restoration requirements.
approach: MIRAGE uses channel-wise functional decomposition assigning CNN, attention, and MLP branches to handle local textures, global context, and channel statistics, plus manifold regularization with SPD contrastive alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with superior efficiency-performance trade-offs, showing strong zero-shot generalization across degradation types.

problem: Adapting single-arm vision-language-action models for bimanual tasks requires substantial bimanual data and fine-tuning, limiting data efficiency.
approach: TwinVLA modularly composes two pretrained single-arm VLA copies into a coordinated bimanual model, leveraging public single-arm data without requiring bimanual pretraining.
contribution: Outperforms comparably-sized monolithic models and narrows the gap to state-of-the-art approaches, establishing modular composition as data-efficient for high-performance bimanual manipulation.

problem: Data-free robustness distillation overlooks robust fairness, causing severe disparity in robustness across categories and instability under different attacks.
approach: FERD adjusts adversarial example proportion and distribution through robustness-guided class reweighting, generates Fairness-Aware Examples via uniformity constraints, and constructs Uniform-Target Adversarial Examples with uniform target constraints.
contribution: Achieves improved fairness and robust stability in adversarial robustness distillation across public datasets through principled proportion and distribution adjustments.

problem: It is unclear whether RLVR truly enhances LLM reasoning or merely boosts sampling efficiency when rewards are based only on answer correctness.
approach: Introduces CoT-Pass@K metric capturing reasoning success via intermediate steps, provides theoretical framework explaining RLVR's incentive mechanism for correct reasoning, and analyzes training dynamics.
contribution: Demonstrates RLVR extends the reasoning boundary for mathematical and coding tasks, with substantial improvements confirmed through extensive evaluations and CoT-Pass@K analysis.

problem: LLM agents for biomedical data science lack comprehensive training environments; commercial and open-source models show large performance disparities.
approach: MedAgentGym provides 72,413 task instances across 129 categories in executable sandboxes with feedback and ground truth, supporting efficient offline and online reinforcement learning with Med-Copilot.
contribution: Med-Copilot achieves +43.02% (offline) and +45.28% (online) RL gains, establishing a cost-effective, privacy-preserving alternative competitive with proprietary LLMs.

problem: Few-shot object detection with vision foundation models suffers from bounding box overfragmentation, producing small false positives instead of complete detections.
approach: FSOD-VFM integrates SAM2, DINOv2, and a universal proposal network, using graph-based diffusion to reweight box confidence scores across a network of predicted boxes for improved granularity.
contribution: Substantially outperforms existing approaches on Pascal-5i, COCO-20i, and CD-FSOD without requiring additional training, achieving 31.6 A on the challenging CD-FSOD dataset.
